text:
devon: Heads-up — our drift detector just flagged a prod vs staging difference for the GPU nodepool sizes. Posting quick diffs and commands I ran.
ops-bot: ALERT: drift-detect/infra-job (drift-detector) found 1 config drift for cluster=redwood-prod — severity=high — inspected resources: module.gpu_pool, k8s/nodepool labels. Link: https://internal.tools/drift/1755012345 
mar ia: Can you paste the terraform plan snippet?
sam: Also wondering if autoscaler touched this overnight.
devon: here's the relevant terraform block from the last apply vs current state we captured:
```
module "gpu_pool" {
-  count = 16
+  count = 48
  gpu_type = "A100"
  taints = ["nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule"]
}
```
devon: and kubectl shows actual nodes in prod:
```
$ kubectl --context=prod get nodes -l nodepool=gpu -o wide | wc -l
48
```
devon: staging is still at 16 nodes.
noah: Who scaled prod manually? That many GPUs is going to blow the budget if it stays.
maria: We have an OPA policy that requires terraform to be source of truth for nodepool count. Why did drift happen?
devon: Oncall did a manual scale-up last night for a long-running research run (they used k8s cluster-autoscaler with manual override). They forgot to update the TF module and the GitOps sync didn't surface it because we only alert on label/taints diffs by default.
sre-jen: That explains it. Our drift detector has a config gap — it compared labels but not count for module.gpu_pool. I'll update the detector to include numeric diffs for critical modules.
maria: Immediate question: reconcile by updating TF to 48 or scale prod back to 16? Which has lower risk?
noah: Prefer updating Terraform if the research team expects the capacity for >24h. If it was a one-off, scale down and enforce a policy change so manual scales create a pull request.
devon: cost estimate: 48 A100 nodes ~ ~ $3.5k/day (ballpark), staging at 16 is ~ $1.2k/day. Not negligible.
sam: Suggestion: create a short freeze on auto-rollouts for prod nodepools until we reconcile, so automation doesn't oscillate.
sre-jen: Agreed. I'll add a temporary gate to the GitOps bot (no auto-sync for nodepool diffs) and create a policy in gatekeeper to block direct `kubectl scale` without a linked PR.
ops-bot: Created issue RD-842: "prod gpu nodepool drift — reconcile + policy hardening" and assigned to devon, label=urgent. https://issues.internal/RD-842
devon: I'll open a terraform PR to bump module.gpu_pool.count -> 48 and add a comment that this came from manual research scale. Will request review from noah and maria.
maria: Also please add a short postmortem in the PR describing why autoscaler override was used and a recommended process.
noah: If PR lands, do not auto-merge. We'll run a canary plan in staging then apply during a maintenance window.
devon: Plan created: `terraform plan -target=module.gpu_pool` shows the change cleanly. I'll kick off the manual apply after approvals.
sam: Also consider adding a periodic similarity check between TF state and live k8s counts — maybe run daily and create an incident if delta > 10%.
sre-jen: On it — I'll add the 10% threshold and roll the detector update in tomorrow's infra-ci job.
mar ia: Thanks all. Tagging @research-team to confirm whether they still need 48 nodes beyond next 24h.
ops-bot: NOTE: GitOps auto-sync suspended for resource=module.gpu_pool until RD-842 resolves.
devon: I'll update RD-842 with the timeline and link to the PR. Thanks 🙏 :warning:
noah: Cool — keep us posted, please.
